links.reason: The verse is the narrator reporting the crowd's names (புனமயிலே, அன்னமே, அமரர்மகள்), not a doctrine; Naladiyar 48 mocks praise of சாந்தும் கோதையும். The two do not make rival claims, and the claim that the epic 'gives it without rebuke' is a view of the narrator not in the Tamil.

Line 4 is repaired and unclear (நிதியது சுரமை), and the verse names no disease, protection or yield; the Kural's five ornaments are held against a verse that says almost nothing of them. The pairing rests on an absence in a doubtful text.
links.text_issue: Line 4 repaired from TSCII leftovers; sense uncertain

links.reason: Verse 101 says only that Somaprabha takes up நற்றவம் and yoga so that வினைகள் தீர; Kural 261 defines தவம் as உற்றநோய் நோன்றல், உயிர்க்குறுகண் செய்யாமை. Neither endurance nor non-harm appears in the verse, so it neither limits nor tests the couplet, and the Kural does not 'fix what the austerity must mean' for it.

The verse has no confinement: she keeps silent (மோனங் கொண்டே) and thinks of her husband while Manasavegan tries மன்னிய நிறை யழிக்க. The word நிறை does match Kural 57 (நிறைகாக்கும் காப்பே தலை), but the note's 'confines her' and 'house of a king' are not in these lines.

Both verses present adornment as skilled craft (கைந்நூற் றிறத்தின்... எந்நூற் றிறமு முணர்வாள்; நிலமறிந் தணிக... நெறியின்), but 2437 does not answer or fulfil 673; it is a second scene of the same kind. The link is a parallel, not a development.

1569 has the jester say modakas fill his belly (மோதகங்கண் முழுகும் பல); 1570 says he has eaten none, they are to be eaten at the festival (இனிப்போய்... தின்னலுறு கின்றன). This is a punchline answering a setup in adjacent verses, not a tension between rival claims.

2124 throws away the sword of meditation (தியானவாள் விட்டெறிந்து) after the karma-kings die; Kural 350 commands பற்றுக... பற்று விடற்கு, holding in order to let go. The tool-then-drop logic is shared, but the Kural's object is the attachment to the passionless one, not meditation, so it is a parallel rather than a qualification.

339 gives a drunk, lustful man reborn as an elephant (காமங் கள்ளுண்டு... ஆனைய தாயினன்); Kural 920 names பெண்டிரும் கள்ளும் கவறும் as the company of the fortune-forsaken. There is no gambling and no word of lost fortune in 339, so 'the rule names his company as the mark of a man fortune has left' is not supported.

77 says only that the sons will serve one man (ஒருவனைச் சேவை பண்ணும்) and does not name him; 81 has Vyala say சிறியன்யா னின்னா னென்றான் on a hidden forehead mark, a verse the marker itself calls uncertain. Reading this as the prophecy beginning to come true is a reconstructed plot.
links.text_issue: 81: speaker and the forehead-eye clause uncertain

links.reason: 2279's warrior says 'for a day like this' (இனையன பட்ட ஞான்றா லிறைவர்கள் நினைப்பது) with the speaker unnamed; Purananuru 290 is a bard bidding the king give toddy to a man whose grandfather died for the king's grandfather (இவற்குஈந்து உண்மதி). The shared lord-feeds-fighter bond is real, but one is not an answer to the other, so 'the warrior's own voice accepting the debt' is invented.

408 (corrupt, ஆசரவச்சுவக் கிரீவன்) has two சேடி rows promised by marriage; 548 (வெள்ளி விலங்கலுங் கொடுத்து) gives Nami the silver mountain. The identification of the two ridges is the marker's, and neither verse says the Vidyadharas are men, so the teaches sentence rests on a claim from outside both.

1998 says one who gives harmful wealth to evil-doers will earn a fruit the sage can only laugh to tell (நகுவ துடைத்தே); 1999 gives the likeness: he is like one who hands great wealth to cruel men and says 'serve me' (வன்கட் பதகர்க்கு... பணிகொண்மி னென்பவ னொத்தான்). The second supplies the reason for the first, turning a rule into a picture of self-harm.

The Tamil does fix the same Thazhumban (ஊணூர் in both), but in Akananuru 227 Unur is a landmark (ஊணூர் உம்பர்) and the comparison is to Marungur's market; only Purananuru 348 compares the girl to ஊணூர். So it is not the same use of one image, and 'stock scale of plenty' is drawn from a single case.

46 (நேராமற் கற்றது கல்வி யன்று) is flagged uncertain, with நேராமல் open to three readings; 8 ranks serving the learned (கற்றாரை வழிபடுதல்) above learning. Calling 46 a 'condition' that 8 develops is one reading of an ambiguous line, and 8 is also marked as differing from the site's verse.

445 defines greatness by the eightfold seeds burnt (அட்டக வித்து வெந்தாம்); 458 returns to the seed (வித்தென்றும் வெந்தால் முளையல தாய்) to say the soul abides without birth in siddhi, deathless. The same speaker uses the image first for what makes the Lord great and then to answer whether release is extinction, so the second extends the first.

1842 speaks of seed still to sow (வித்திடற் பால தென்றான்); 2005 says the wealth of austerity grows in kinds and many (இரண்டும் பலவு மியலாய்ப் பெருகு) but has no seed or sowing word. That the sage is answering the king's image is an assumption, and the verses are far apart.

2000: gifts of one who knows the principles lift him among the best gods (உத்தம தேவரு ளுய்க்கும்); 2047: householders who give, shun wine and flesh and keep faith become உயர்ந்தவர்க்கு ளுயர்ந்துளராய். The ethical widening is real, but 2047 does not 'name who these are' (2000's giver is the one who has grasped the tattvas), and both verses are marked uncertain.
links.text_issue: Both flagged uncertain; 2047 line 3 construction unclear

links.reason: 2065 says the highest gods are கோனிலா with none greater, a statement about heavenly ranks; Tirumanthiram 266 contrasts ripened and resolute souls with the proud, and 'ruling his heaven' (ஈசன் துறக்கமது ஆள்வர்) is no claim about a lord over gods. No incompatible claim about the same thing is stated, and both verses are flagged uncertain.

1448 has Tivittan say the boast was made 'from a hilltop among your band' and ask whether it holds before his face (குன்றின்மே லிருந்து நீநின் குழுவினுண் மொழிவ தல்லால்); Kural 664 says சொல்லுதல் எளிய, செயல் அரிது. The packet shows no test of action, so 'the bragger is made to act and his weapons fail' is not in the evidence.

402 (name corrupt) foretells that Kesava will take Ashvagriva's life through a girl; 632 has the astrologer say the youngest of the princes will be an ancient foe (இளையான் தமக்... தொல்பகை). 'Same prince' is the marker's identification across two uncertain verses; 632 does not name Podanam or the prince.
links.text_issue: 402 line 3 name corrupt; 632 speaker split unclear

links.reason: 243 has the queen long to go in the sky and the king ask ministers; 249 gives the cause (the being in her womb) and a flying mantra. That is a real answer to a problem, but lines 1-2 are hard and 'the flight is a sign of the child's nature' goes beyond the Tamil.

The images differ: the lamp's புகை (NKK 3) and the moon's spot (விமலந்தனக் கில்ல தன்றே, Neelakesi 6); only the apologetic function is shared. Two poems cannot show that this was 'a stock gesture of the Jain poets'.

1557 only compares the hero's setting out to men who leave dancers and wife (துறந்துசெல் பவர்போற்); 27 narrates his final renunciation (அரசு அஞ்சித் துறந்த வாறும்). The shared word துறந்து does not make the simile a rehearsal of the end; that is read in from the patikam.

262 shows Kattiyangaran chaining the king's kin and winning followers with wealth (நிகளம் மூழ்கி... இரு நிதி முகந்து நல்கி); Tirumanthiram 245's second half (போந்திவ் வுலகைப் பிறர்க்கொள்ளத் தாங்கொள்ள) is uncertain and is about a king, not a minister's coup. The 'verdict of blame matches a doctrine' is not stated by either verse.

1482 makes the brow a bent bow (நடுவொசி நோன்சிலைப் புருவத் தாற்புடைத்து) among hair, eyes and breasts; Kural 1086 says her eyes would not hurt if the brows did not bend (கொடும்புருவம் கோடா மறைப்பின்). Brow and bending are shared, but the epic does not answer the couplet; 'the idea that the brows might have held the eyes back' is not in 1482.

In YK 79 a white hair on the crown (மயி ருச்சி வெண்மை) is seen in a mirror; in Silappathikaram 28, Maadalan says நரைமுதிர் யாக்கை நீயுங் கண்டனை as a passing remark before the doctrine of rebirth. Grey hair as a sign of age is stock; the contrast with Asokan acting depends on later verses not in the pair.

1109 has கூற்றத்தைக் கொம்மை கொட்டி குலத்தொடு முடியு மென்பார்; Kural 894 has கூற்றத்தைக் கையால் விளித்தற்றால், with only கூற்றத்தை in common, so the women do not 'apply the couplet'. Nothing in the verse calls the king weak or Civakan strong, so 'strength a matter of worth not office' is added.

2127: Death and Desire leave and he gains kevala-light (காலர் காமர் கையகல... கேவலப்பே ரொளி); Tirumanthiram 345: he burned Death in yoga fire (காலனைக் காய்ந்தங்கி யோகமாய்). These are two accounts of overcoming Death, not claims that exclude each other, and 345 never says 'god's fire' in the words.

Purananuru 119 compares the giver to நிழலில் நீளிடைத் தனிமரம்; Kural 216 to பயன்மரம் உள்ளூர்ப் பழுத்தற்றால். The tree-as-giver image is shared and the placement contrast (town centre, shadeless road) is real, but the poem does not extend the couplet; it is a same_image pair.

2099 narrates the king giving army and earth to his sons (சிறுவர்க் கீந்துபோய்) with a thousand kings taking off crowns; Tirumanthiram 168 does not address a king but says to join செல்வன் before wealth passes to others. 'Handing over without a god' is silent on any vow or lord, so the epic neither meets nor refuses the urging.

269 begins ஆகவெனின் ஆகும்... அழிகவெனின் அழியும், so the power is spoken (எனின்), which is close to the Kural's நிறைமொழி; the note's 'in his will, where the couplet puts it in the word' misreads this. The verse also adds விதியின், but that shifts the claim without refuting Kural 28.

131 closes with the residents eating விருந்தொடும், among silver hearths and gold vessels; Kural 81 says all household life is for விருந்தோம்பி வேளாண்மை. The verse gives no sign that the city 'will soon fall', so the contrast of purpose and luxury is partly invented.

123: the king, with the sword in hand (கரத்து வாளும்), stops his own rage after reflection; Kural 301 says anger guarded where it can act is real guarding (செல்லிடத்துக் காப்பான்). It is a clean instance of the rule, so it illustrates rather than extends it, and the Kural gains no new case or limit.

Line 1 of 2573 is corrupt (நீக்கிப் யாய) and the friend is not named, so 'the dog who became a god' is a reconstruction from 945. The verse sets up a gold likeness and a dance, with no word of births, whereas Kural 107 turns on எழுமை எழுபிறப்பும் உள்ளுவர்.

539's astrologer says her destined husband lives in Rajamapuram (இராசமா புரத்த தென்றான்); 753 has Padumukan call her பத்தினிப் பாவை of Civakan and ask whether kings may contend. The prophecy-and-outcome link is real, but 753 never refers to the horoscope or fate, so 'defended as karpu rather than the stars' is a gloss.

604 wishes வான்றரு வளம் and கற்பினிற் றிரித லின்றி as separate benedictions, with no link; the marker notes the verse does not make one the cause of the other. Kural 55 says the wife commands the rain (பெய்யெனப் பெய்யும் மழை), so the pairing contrasts the Kural with a connection the verse never draws.

96's drake leaves the flock and is likened to an ascetic (யோகொடு கறை அற முயல்வது), while 1624's drake pleads and embraces (சிறகாற் புல்லிப் பணிந்து). The reversal of one image is real, but 1624 mentions no Civakan, so 'draws Civakan back into longing' is not in the text.

194 gathers சிலம்பு, அரவ மேகலை, கோதை, நோக்கம், ஊறு and calls the joy அரிது உலப்பு; Kural 1101 says the five senses find their objects in the one woman. The 'cost' appears only in 198, outside the packet, and the verse names no king, so the 'setting where completeness becomes danger' is not in 194.

1485's queens bar desire with கற்பு வேலி and நிறையின் தாழ், and நிறை is the very word of Kural 57. That makes the self-made guard a case of the rule, but it follows the rule rather than limiting it, and the verse is marked uncertain; 'a test of the couplet' is overstated.

1581 has the jester say the grove has no guard (சிறிதேனுங் காவ லின்று); 1582 has the king answer that many warriors keep the wall (மறவோர் பலர்காப்பர்). This is a question and reply within a joke, and the 'monkeys' resolution in 1583-4 is not in the packet.

356 crowns Gomukhan (மன்னுகோ முகனுக்கு), whom the marker cannot place as son or minister; 162 crowns குமரன் before going forth. 'The crown goes outside the family' and 'to whoever can rule it' are therefore not stated, and a shared event type does not qualify one by the other.

2815 says Indra and a small monkey alike eat the fruit of deeds (வினைப்பயத்தை யுண்ணும்) and ends with the Lord's text (இறைவ னூலும்); Tirumanthiram 105 puts the Lord beyond இருவினை. The Jain verse does not say that no one stands outside deeds, and 105 is marked uncertain, so an incompatible claim is not stated by either.

139 says the Jina's shrines everywhere keep the city's wealth (ஆக்கம் அறாதது); Tirumanthiram 518 says if pujas stop kings suffer and rain (வாரி/மாரி) and theft follow. Both tie shrines to prosperity, but the Jain verse is praise and the Saiva one a threat, so 'doctrine rather than praise' and a Jain 'same causal link' overstate a shared topic.
180 ends with arrows shutting out the sun (அக்கதிர் மறைத்தவே) and 181 describes the field of ruin (வீழவும்... ஆடவும்). This is battle in story order, and 181 does not answer or reverse 180.
